# localmelo

> localmelo is a local personal agent that runs tasks with tools (shell, Python, files, MCP servers) and memory on a model server the user runs (any OpenAI-compatible server, Ollama) or on a cloud API (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, NVIDIA). It offers the `melo` command, which returns a fixed exit code per run and prints one JSON line with `--output-format json`, an experimental Python API, and an HTTP gateway on 127.0.0.1. It is pre-alpha: interfaces may change before v0.1.0.

- Install from a clone named `localmelo` with Python 3.11+: `uv sync --extra gateway`, then run `uv run melo` in the clone (`melo` is not on PATH). MIT license. localmelo never downloads, starts or serves models.
- One task: `melo --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 --chat-model MODEL --output-format json --timeout 300 -- "TASK"`; `--reasoning legacy|drop|replay|compress|compress+replay` (default `legacy`, unchanged) chooses whether a reply's reasoning is sent back, with `--reasoning-field auto|reasoning_content|reasoning` (replay and compress+replay), `--replay-turns N` and `--note-writer auto|heuristic` (compress modes: each reply becomes a RAM-only note and its drafts), `--retriever auto|off|bm25|llm|embedding`, `--recall-at start,attempt,step,tool`, `--recall-k 1..10`, `--recall-kinds note,draft,thought,digest,reflection,long`, `--recall-placement tool|message`, `--recall-min-score 0..1`, `--retrieval-extra-body JSON`, `--admit-on-outcome on|off` and `--keep-decision-text` (R6-lite's typed long store: a candidate is admitted by rehearsal, a user request (which also admits the fact after its marker) or statement, or the outcome switch; one decision per action; `--keep-decision-text` is refused in the UI), and `long_term.db` `user_version` 1 with the typed columns and `decisions` (legacy migrates in place, rows and search unchanged); `melo-retrieve --export-store DIR|FILE`, `--export-decisions DIR|FILE`, `--route CANDIDATES.jsonl --memory-dir DIR` score the store offline (a directory with no store prints zero and exits 0); R5: compress recalls at start/attempt/step by default; auto = embedding if configured, else llm at start/attempt and bm25 at step/tool; tool is never on unless named; a step's recall can include a superseded note or thought chunk of an evicted turn, and `memory_stats.recall_empty` counts a recall that found nothing; legacy refuses these flags); `--workspace DIR` makes the run work in that folder: file tools stay inside it and `shell_exec`/`python_exec` start there (default: the current folder; a path that is not a folder exits 2 with one line); a direct run offers `file_read`, `file_write` and `python_exec`, and `--builtins all` (or `--builtins shell_exec`) adds `shell_exec` (off by default); exit 0 completed, 1 crashed or a configuration error, 2 any other status or a usage error. Bare `melo` in a terminal opens the interactive UI (a first run asks for a model server and model and saves them, as `ollama` when the server answers `GET /api/version` like Ollama, else as `vllm`; thinking, tool calls and progress shown live, approvals (with a diff for an overwritten file), `/model`, `/backend`, `/verbose`, `/thinking`, `/expand`, `/progress`, `/approvals`, `/status`, `/mcp`, `/retry`); `--mcp-config FILE` or the config's top-level `mcp_config` loads MCP servers; without a TTY it exits 2. `melo --serve` starts the gateway. Agents: do not run bare `melo` in a pty under the user's HOME, and use direct mode in scripts.
- Fixed prefix is opt-in via `[agent] fixed_prefix = true` or `--fixed-prefix on`; `off` overrides the config. Local date and UTC offset freeze per run; `all` freezes sorted schemas while `retrieve` remains dynamic. `prefix_cache.schema_changes` counts changes, not measured server misses; cached tokens appear only when reported for planning/reflection.
- Context accounting is opt-in: set `[agent] context_window`, `output_reserve`, `safety_margin`, or matching flags, all positive with window > reserve + margin. It fits over-budget planning/reflection requests on a copy, or ends `context_budget_exceeded`; it does not enforce a generation cap. Estimates, including the image allowance, are not bounds. See [configuration](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/configuration.md#context-accounting).
- Reasoning/recall in sessions: interactive flags `--reasoning`, `--reasoning-field`, `--replay-turns`, `--note-writer`, `--retriever`, `--recall-*`, `--retrieval-extra-body` override `[agent]`/`[retrieval]` defaults; a `--base-url` session ignores those defaults. Native Ollama refuses an explicit reasoning-field flag. Console sessions honor configured reasoning (default `legacy`) while keeping gateway tool mode; legacy `/v1` is unchanged. `/model`/`/backend` keep mode/conversation and RAM-only notes/drafts; replay-required drop refusal retains the old Agent and MCP state. Session replay scope is window; pairs restore no old thinking, window restores retained redacted thinking; current mode wins over old outcome config. Notes remain RAM-only, not restored from turns.note. `[agent] tool_env` lists extra inherited shell/Python variable names (valid ASCII names, missing skipped, save names only); SSH_AUTH_SOCK grants SSH-agent access and proxy variables may expose credentials. Defaults expose nothing new; --base-url ignores it; MCP env is separate. See [configuration](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/configuration.md#tool-environment).
- Attempt digests skip task headings; `verified` requires a passing test runner or a check referencing an earlier written file. A failed last check removes verification.
- Compress-mode heuristic notes extract up to 12 keyed facts from visible replies without a note block; questions, plans and negated/cancelled statements are not positive facts, and CJK-only keys are not extracted. A unique best source wins; ties and conflicts remain unsourced. Self-work frames are filtered unless a keyed content clause follows; completed outcome-admitted digests are exempt. See [Memory](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/memory.md).
- Worker sessions: direct `--save-session [TITLE] -- TASK` records one turn; `--parent-run ID` needs it. `--import-session dsh-jsonl FILE [--title TITLE]` imports once by content hash. Read via `GET /api/sessions?kind=worker` (filters `status`, `source`, `parent_run`; `cursor` / `next_cursor`) and worker detail/turns; no writes or live follow. Workspace defaults to cwd; `session.tokens` is total tokens, `meta.usage` is the usage map; SQLite may create WAL/SHM sidecars on reads. Regex redaction is not a guarantee against arbitrary printed secrets; recognizable sensitive file reads are omitted. Thinking follows session retention.
- The web workspace offers `#/workers` (server-filtered and cursor-paged) and `#/workers/<id>` (read-only snapshot, explicit refresh, no worker SSE or write controls). Worker detail `tokens` is null without integer completion tokens; chat-only details and submission lookup return 404 for worker-only IDs. See the console guide and API v2 reference below.
- The `/` workspace uses `/api` for connection settings, connection testing, a browser-local theme, tools/grants/memory/runs drawer, earlier turns, failure controls and per-tab outbox recovery; console sessions use `RememberingPolicy` to ask before `file_write` and `python_exec` and render approval cards; legacy `/v1` has no approval policy.
- Saved terminal chats: `melo -c` resumes the newest eligible chat in this workspace; `melo -r [ID|TITLE]`, `/sessions [filter]` and `/resume [id|title]` resolve or pick one. Picker filtering, Tab folder/all-folders and Esc preserve the draft. Startup selection precedes the named banner. Resuming keeps current model/workspace and `/verbose`/`/thinking`, clears grants and explains restored memory (`[sessions] resume_mode = "pairs"` default or `"window"`); `/retry` keeps stored typed text and `/expand` reads persisted tool output. Cross-window changes reload before sending; busy/deleted sessions keep drafts. Only CLI chats with finished turns are offered; no web/scheduler sessions. `-c` and `-r` are mutually exclusive and interactive-only. Direct parsing/output stays unchanged; put task text after `--`.
- Terminal session tools: `/title [text]` shows/sets a title (kept until lazy first-turn creation); idle-only `/undo` forgets the newest finished turn, keeps typed history and never reverses file changes; a committed undo reports success even after Esc, and `/retry` re-runs that undone turn without undoing the previous one. `/usage` includes undone work, leaves missing/running counters unknown and reflows on narrow terminals; `/memory` inspects a copied, cleaned working window and explains the actual resume mode, without model calls or memory writes. `/copy [turn]` copies stored redacted Markdown without thinking, preserving indentation/newlines with bounded turn reads, not wrapped terminal output; local macOS uses bounded `/usr/bin/pbcopy`, SSH/other platforms/failure request OSC 52 (terminal support varies). Tests must fake native copying: temporary HOME does not isolate the OS clipboard.
- Tools run with the user's permissions and no sandbox; `python_exec` code runs in a child process, killed at its time limit. The gateway has no authentication and must stay on 127.0.0.1. Only `interactive` mode offers `shell_exec` by default; a direct run, the gateway, a console session and the Python API's default `mode="python"` register `file_read`, `file_write` and `python_exec`, and `--builtins all` (or naming `shell_exec`) turns the shell on in a direct run or the Python API, after which it runs without an approval unless that run passes `approval=` (a `python`-mode run can). `AgentOptions(mode="direct"|"interactive"|"gateway"|"python")`; an explicit `builtins` set always wins, except that a gateway still refuses `shell_exec`, named or not.

- `[gateway] workspace` is empty (console default `~/localmelo-workspace`) or an absolute/`~/` path that must not resolve to `/` or home.

## Docs

- [localmelo for agents](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/for-agents.md): the one page an agent needs: install, CLI, Python API, HTTP, results, config, tools, memory, gotchas and rules.
- [Quickstart](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/start/quickstart.md): install, run a first task, save a configuration and start the gateway.
- [Command-line reference](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/cli.md): `melo` modes, options, output, exit codes and signals; [interactive UI guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/terminal.md) covers keys, commands and approvals.
- [Run results](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/run-results.md): run statuses, the fields of the JSON line and `RunResult`, and retries.
- [Python API](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/python-api.md): `Agent`, `AgentOptions`, `RunResult` and methods; [Python guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/python.md) covers stopping, approvals and workspaces.
- [Events](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/events.md): the events a Python run reports, their order, fields and rules.
- [Session guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/sessions.md) and [sessions reference](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/sessions.md): conversations kept in SQLite (experimental Python API): turns, statuses, message ids, resume, approvals for a person and the event stream; `SessionRunner(..., progress=True)` stores a turn's `run.progress`, `run_turn`/`start_turn` take `routine=`, and `build_session_agent` can wrap the providers the Agent is built with (`wrap_llm`/`wrap_embedding`).
- [Gateway guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/gateway.md), [web console](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/web-console.md) and [HTTP v1 reference](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/http-v1.md): startup, loopback guard, workspace and legacy routes.
- [API v2](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/api-v2.md): the web console's `/api` routes (health, settings, key-status, connection test, model listing, sessions, turns, SSE events, blobs, submission lookups, the writes that create a session and start, retry, stop and approve its turns, its scheduler level and typing heartbeat, scheduler task creation, inspection and control, and the details: tools, grants, memory and runs), the one error shape, the 1 MiB body limit and JSON content-type rule, a [create-run-approve script](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/api-client.md), and the additive-only promise; loopback only. S3a.2 task workers: they share the gate, disable memory, omit `shell_exec`, and have at most four resident workers. Rows persist, but startup fails surviving nonterminal tasks with `gateway restarted; recovery arrives in S3b`; full recovery, deadlines and accounting are deferred. Invalid workspaces fail at run/resume. Pause records pending P5 while running providers and tools finish; a held plan, reflection or undelivered approval can park, save an evidence card and release its slot. Resume uses that card and re-asks withdrawn approvals. A task paused before start starts no worker until resumed. Resume restores prior priority from a durable snapshot or computed P2 without one; an unpaused task returns 409 `not_paused`. Unsaved parks retry with the fence closed, then interrupt with a card; while finalization cannot be stored, resume and stop return 503. Cleanup failure quarantines the worker and retains its slot until restart. PATCH `first` is rejected with 400 until S6b. `request_key` makes creation idempotent.
- [Tools reference](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/tools.md) and [Tools and MCP guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/tools-mcp.md): built-ins, MCP configuration, permissions and checks.
- [Memory reference](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/memory.md), [memory guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/memory.md) and [memory concepts](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/concepts/memory.md): storage, inspection, reset and the memory layers.
- [Configuration reference](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/configuration.md), [setup guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/configure.md) and [model servers](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/model-servers.md): wizard, backends and configuration keys.
- [Set up an embedding model](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/embedding.md): long-term memory's embedding backend, the probe that proves one works, and server commands for Ollama, oMLX, vLLM, SGLang and MLC.
- [Troubleshooting](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/troubleshooting.md): error messages and how to fix them.

## Optional

- [How localmelo works](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/concepts/how-it-works.md): the run loop, reflection, memory and timeouts.
- [Evaluations](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/project/evaluations.md): the controlled comparisons behind the defaults, such as the reflection gate (one model, 12 coding exercises).
- [Offline retrieval](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/retrieval.md): `melo-retrieve`, which compares memory retrievers offline; runs do not use it.
- [Procedural memory](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/concepts/procedures.md): the steps of recurring tasks, which every run records at its end (`procedures.db` with persistence on) and which `run.progress` events report to a Python caller and `melo` draws as a progress line on a terminal; `localmelo.support.progress_line.format_past` gives that line's past facts and items alone; `melo-procedures` replays the progress rules offline.
- [Scheduler](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/scheduler.md): the scheduling policy core and its simulator, for maintainers; the gateway's web chats and the console's sessions are gated (`[scheduler] policy`, default `off`), and it reads the shared GPU lock and the battery, holding chats while a foreign session holds the lock under `[scheduler] lock_gate = "wait"` (default `record`, which only records); direct runs and the CLI are unchanged.
- [Developer guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/en/developers.html): the repository layout, the development setup, the tests and checks, adding a backend, a built-in tool or a check, and how to send a change.
- [Changelog](https://github.com/localmelo/localmelo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): notable changes; there is no release yet, so all are under Unreleased.
- [Repository](https://github.com/localmelo/localmelo): source code, issues and the contributing guide.
